intended_object: An auxiliary open set used only in this file: the domain on which the second projection Spec S → Spec(R ×_T S) is restricted. It is the open complement Spec S \ V(ker g) of the zero locus of ker g. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and how it is used in `sndOpenMap` and `isOpenImmersion_sndOpenMap`.
explanation:
The body is `kernelComplement g`, which is the open set `(PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (ker g))ᶜ` in `Spec S`. It also takes an argument `_f` that it never uses; that argument is there only so that `sndSource f g` matches the signatures of `sndOpenMap f g` and the other definitions in the file.

The definition is just a name for the source of the restricted second projection. Its only role is to state and prove the file's results: that the projection is an open immersion on this set (`isOpenImmersion_sndOpenMap`), and what its image is (`range_sndOpenMap`). It is not a standard notion from the literature in its own right, so it is best classed as a technical device.

Judged as what the docstring and module documentation describe, "the complement of ker g", it is correct. The set Spec S \ V(ker g) is exactly that complement, and the file proves that the restricted map is an open immersion with image the complement of ker(pullbackFst). There are no degenerate cases to worry about: if g is injective, then ker g = ⊥, V(⊥) is all of Spec S, and the open set is empty, which is the correct answer. Nothing in the body calls for a broader setting either: it works for arbitrary commutative rings in a single universe, which is all the `Spec` / `CommRingCat` setup requires.
